Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

He speaks English **good**.
solution:
The correct answer is '**well**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The adverb "**well**" is used to describe how someone performs an action, specifically in a skillful or effective manner.
 
• In this context, "He speaks English" requires an adverb to modify the verb "speaks" appropriately.
 
• **Option 1 (very good)** is incorrect because "good" is an adjective, and the phrase would still be grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 2 (nicely)** is incorrect because it does not convey the intended meaning of proficiency in speaking English.
 
• **Option 3 (fluently)** is incorrect because the sentence does not explicitly refer to fluency but rather to speaking skill in general.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"He speaks English **well**__."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "very good"** is not suitable as "good" is an adjective and cannot modify the verb "speaks" directly.
 
• **Option 2: "nicely"** is grammatically correct but does not convey the intended meaning of skill or proficiency.
 
• **Option 3: "fluently"** specifically refers to the ability to speak a language smoothly and accurately, which is not the focus of the original sentence.
